_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002). Never add tasks for individual worlds here

tasks.title: Windows on every face and storey the evidence shows
tasks.notes: Cause: a spec's facades table usually lists one face per building, and Build.windows punches glass only on listed faces and storeys. Even listed faces are nearly blank above storey 1: SUSU north storey 1 82%, storey 2 3%, storey 3 0%; West east 4-8%; Retail south 8%/3%; Jubilee south 34/25/24%. Covers issue I-004 (glazing far below the photos: windows only on the faces the spec lists), snag S-006. Scope: (1) the dry run lists every exposed face and storey with its glazed share, marking faces with no facade row 'no evidence read' (report, not a gate); (2) the designer brief asks for a facade row for every exposed face, read from street photos and the aerial; where no evidence shows a face, copy the nearest read face and say so in the spec notes. Done when dry runs for susu_w33830305, west_w34391673 and retail_w33830236 list every face with no unexplained gap. Check line S-006: each building's windows look like the photos on every face, upper storeys included. Not verified: whether the low upper-storey shares come from misread photos or omitted rows; check first when picked up. Touches feature_build.py like #125 and #126; sequence them. One regression test only; no new gates or lints.

tasks.title: Window panes need a solid frame
tasks.notes: Cause: Build.windows punches glass_pane into any listed face with no framing check (doors have door_frame_issues; windows have no equivalent), so on stepped or diagonal walls a pane meets open air. Covers issue I-013 (glass panes on diagonal walls have no frame), snag S-007. Scope: place a pane only where the finished build has solid wall on both sides along the wall line and above and below; otherwise keep the wall block. The dry run prints the count of panes skipped this way, per face. Done when dry runs for susu_w33830305 and Jubilee report no pane beside air. Check line S-007: every glass pane on SUSU's and Jubilee's diagonal walls has solid blocks all round it. Touches feature_build.py like #125, #126 and #130; sequence them. One regression test only; no new gates or lints.

tasks.title: Roof and facade detail in the building spec
tasks.notes: Cause: the building spec has no vocabulary for roof or facade detail and feature_build places none. rules/building-review.md already asks the designer to list roof greeblies per roof from the aerial (plant boxes, vents, louvred vents, skylights, solar panels, lift overruns, parapets) and names a --greeblies feature follow-up step, but no script or lib has --greeblies (probably lost in the move from the Refine donor; not confirmed). Covers issue I-006 (no roof or facade detail), snags S-009 and S-016. Owner decision (2026-10-27): detail lives in the building spec, not a separate pass, so undo/redo of a building takes its detail with it. Scope: a per-label details table in the spec, each entry a kind, position and size: roof (plant room, vent, louvred vent, skylight, solar panel, lift overrun), facade (drainpipe, sign, canopy, ledge, fascia band); a small block recipe per kind in feature_build, placed after the shell; positions from the aerial (roofs) and street photos (facades), heights of large roof plant from lidar; the designer brief points at building-review and fills details; replace the dead --greeblies reference in the rules with the table; dry run prints each detail and its source. Done when a dry run of SUSU, West or Retail places listed roof and facade details, including Retail's entrance canopy (in its spec notes, never built). Check line S-009, S-016: each building in 48,-44 shows the roof plant and facade detail visible on the aerial and photos. Size l: may split into roof detail and facade detail. Blocked by #125 and #126: details sit on the roofs, and all touch feature_build.py. One regression test per part; no new gates or lints.

tasks.title: Rebuild fixtures for undo tests
tasks.notes: Cause: undo tests hand-roll stage and modifies setup, and missed rebuilds of a layer over itself until the #123 check refused a real ground undo (2026-10-27, Highfield 48,-44). Deliver one test helper in journal_testkit that sets up a ghost base plus N rebuilds of a layer (same, wider, narrower), so undo tests cover rebuilt layers without per-test setup. Known traps: 'ghost-ground' is not an apply stage (use other), and a later build must list the base in modifies. Also covers the interleaved-build case the check refuses today (fails closed, documented in _before_footprints). Add a property test: apply N rebuilds of a layer with NO base owner underneath, then undo them all; the world must equal the start. (A bent fixture in the 2026-10-27 undo-check fix hid exactly this.)

tasks.title: Undo a whole cell in order
tasks.notes: Cause: purging a cell was done by hand and ran undo passes in the wrong order (ground before features); a refusal then halted the chain. Deliver one element_undo command that undoes everything above ghost in a cell in the fixed order (decor, trees, features, ground), stops at the first refusal and reports what is left. Dry run by default, --apply to write, under the site lock.

tasks.title: List cells with non-ghost builds
tasks.notes: Cause: finding what sits above the ghost baseline meant parsing registry/journal.jsonl by hand (cell_registry status takes one cell). Deliver a cell_registry view that names every cell with anything above ghost (ground generated, trees, decor, features) and counts of each, so a purge can be counted in one call.

tasks.title: Purge scope: everything above ghost
tasks.notes: Cause: the purge skill offers element, cell and project, so 'purge the non-ghost stuff' was first read as the project reset, which also wipes ghost. Add a fourth scope to the purge skill: count from the new cells view, undo cell by cell with the new whole-cell command, then retire records and prove each cell is ghost only.

tasks.title: Fix stale command examples in the steering docs
tasks.notes: Cause: AGENTS.md shows site_lock.py run without --world, which the script requires, and nothing points at where tests live (lib/<category>/test_*.py, scripts/test_*.py, run via scripts/run_tests.py --only <stem>). Fix the lock example and add one pointer for test locations. Docs-only; can commit straight to main.

tasks.title: Cell-pass undo restores the world before the first build
tasks.notes: Cause: with no owner underneath, _prepare_undo restores the prior blob of the LATEST targeted build, so undoing a layer rebuilt over itself leaves the first build's blocks instead of the world before either (seen in the undo test with no ghost base, 2026-10-27). The #123 before_<plan> check is a second oracle that disagrees whenever a plan has several live builds; the 2026-10-27 fix only moved it to the earliest covering snapshot. Deliver: per position, restore the prior from the earliest targeted build that touched it, so the journal alone is correct; then make the snapshot check read the same source or reduce it to pit detection (also removes the interleaved-build false refusal noted in _before_footprints).

tasks.title: Cell-orchestrator skill plans features before building a cell
tasks.notes: Cause: the 2026-10-27 overnight run took `cell_registry.py next` as complete, so cells 48,-45 and 49,-45 went ground, trees, decor with no feature step although their maps hold many buildings (ground skipped ~5,400 building-footprint columns in 49,-45) and were logged complete. Deliver: in .claude/skills/cell-orchestrator/SKILL.md add a per-cell preflight (`cell_registry.py propose-features --cell <c> --record` before ground) and a completion gate: not complete until every footprint the ground report skipped is covered by a planned and landed feature; if features exist on the map but none are planned, stop and say so. Also add to the overnight stop list: the same patrol flag repeating across features. Docs-only; can commit straight to main.

tasks.title: next refuses to move past ground on a cell with unplanned building footprints
tasks.notes: Cause: next only offers registry items, so a cell with buildings but no recorded features is indistinguishable from a cell with no buildings and steps ground to trees to decor (2026-10-27, cells 48,-45 and 49,-45). Deliver: when a cell's ground layer skipped building footprints and no plan_feature covers them, next returns a needs-feature-plan item (or runs propose-features --record itself) instead of the trees layer. Test: a fixture cell with one footprint and no features.

tasks.title: verify errors on landed ground whose skipped footprints no feature covers
tasks.notes: Cause: verify only warned about missing specs and decision records, so a cell with half its footprint unbuilt passed with 0 errors (2026-10-27). Deliver: verify reports an error per landed ground layer whose skipped building-footprint columns are not covered by any planned or landed feature, naming the uncovered buildings.

tasks.title: Status pages and morning report show unbuilt footprint per cell
tasks.notes: Cause: morning and site_pages called 48,-45 and 49,-45 complete when about half of 49,-45 was still empty footprint. Deliver: each cell row and the morning report show built vs unbuilt footprint area and the names of unbuilt buildings; a cell with unbuilt footprint cannot show as Completed.

tasks.title: Feature doors land in a one-block vestibule that patrol flags door_to_wall
tasks.notes: Cause: feature_build lays storey floors every 3 blocks from a median-ground level but places each door on its own wall column's lidar ground, so the door's inside cell is floor or solid; 6 flags in the world after 2026-10-27 (jubilee 1, susu 3, west 2). Doors also fall back to one leaf when no pair cell is free (42-B, 57-A, 40-A/B, 18-A). Deliver: tie storey floors to local ground at each door, or clear the inside cell; then a re-apply of the three specs gives 0 patrol flags and keeps two-leaf doors where the spec asks for them.

tasks.title: Decor garden-boundary reads tree canopy as a hedge
tasks.notes: Cause: in 49,-45 decor the aerial hedge reading took the east wood's canopy (x6371..6381, z-5751..-5735) as a garden hedge on Broadlands Road plots and placed 52 oak_leaves, 3 columns on the brick path; a designer spec cannot override it (2026-10-27). Deliver: ignore canopy pixels (use the nDSM tree mask) and treat brick paths like roads; designer spec can veto a detected hedge. Then redo 49,-45 decor.

tasks.title: Facade plan with entrances: the designer accounts for every portal
tasks.notes: Cause: doors are placed at the wall cell nearest a portal point (portals.framed, DOOR_REACH, #114) and the spec's optional `doors` map is rarely filled, so leaf count, face, canopy and floor height are guessed per door (S-021 sunk 42-B door, S-023 57-A on the wrong face, 40-A single not double). Deliver: a per-face facade plan in the building spec (storeys, glazing, entrances with leaf count, canopy or covered area, steps, floor height against outside ground; room for roof edge and detail). Portals are inputs to it, not a stage: the designer brief shows every portal on the footprint with its photo and position when it has one, and each must be placed or declared unresolved with a reason. Each entrance records its source (given coordinate or register entry, photo read, inference) and confidence. Portals are best effort: a world with no portal register still gets entrances from street-level photos. Relates to #130 (windows on every face), #131 (window frames) and #132 (roof and facade detail): decide whether they become fields of this plan or follow it. Check: 57-A is a single door on the side face under a covered area; 40-A shows double doors; 42-B sits at ground level; a portal left unresolved is listed in the plan and the cell view.

tasks.title: Build reads the facade plan; remove the old portal door path everywhere
tasks.notes: Deliver: feature doors and entrances are built from the facade plan (#145) only. Cleanup is part of the task, not a follow-up: remove the nearest-wall-cell door chooser (feature_build.py framed / DOOR_REACH), the legacy front/rear spruce default, the per-portal `doors` map and its spec docs, and scripts/door_audit.py's assumptions about them; keep scripts/portals.py and the register as an evidence reader feeding the designer. Update every place that still tells an agent or designer to put a door at the portal or to use `doors`: rules/craftsmanship.md (ENTRANCES), rules/feature-builds.md, rules/building-review.md, rules/evidence-order.md, rules/rules-context.md, .claude/skills/redo, lib/journal/cell_features.py and lib/evidence/evidence_sheet.py output, bakeoff scenarios and checks that rely on the old door spec, and the tests. Gate: a grep for the removed names (framed, DOOR_REACH, the `doors` key, 'door at every portal') finds nothing outside tasks/done.json and history; unit tests cover entrances read from the plan, including unresolved portals. Door row is set from outside ground so doors cannot sit below it (I-017). Covers I-018 and I-017. Check: the 57-A, 40-A and 42-B checks in #145 hold after a rebuild.
